newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian insurer says 96 pre-tax profit up 7.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian insurer says 96 pre-tax profit up 7.3 pct.

text.p: Croatia's biggest insurance company, state-owned Croatia Osiguranje d.d., said it had recorded a 2.2 percent increase in premium income and pre-tax profit had risen 7.3 percent, reversing five years of decline.
The company's chief executive, Suad Rizvanbegovic, told the annual shareholders meeting the pre-tax profit grew to 34.3 million kuna on a total turnover of 2.3 billion.

Turnover and operating costs were five percent lower than in 1995 due to a change in book-keeping procedures, Rizvanbegovic said. But premium income grew for the first time since 1990. Life insurance income grew at the sharpest rate of 54 percent, while car insurance, which accounts for almost half the company's income, was up 0.5 percent on last year.
Rizvanbegovic qualified that as a success, given the tough competition by small private companies especially in those two segments of the market.

Dividends rose 69 percent compared to last year. The company will pay 112 kuna dividend per A-series issue, held by individuals, or eight percent of its nominal value and 65 kuna per B-series share, held by companies, or 4.6 percent of its value. Both issues have a nominal price of 1,400 kuna and were traded at 1,250 kuna on the Zagreb Stock Exchange on Tuesday.
Croatia Osiguranje d.d. is 77.5 percent owned by the state while other companies hold 19.7 percent and individuals the remaining 2.8 percent.
